summaries.AB 1: Requires the state to consider updating wildfire building hardening regulations by 2030 and every five years thereafter, including property mitigation and community wide programs.
summaries.AB 1007: Cuts the Permit Streamlining Act deadline for a responsible agency to approve or disapprove a project from 90 to 45 days, subject to the bill’s exceptions.
summaries.AB 1021: Revises when housing is an allowed use on land owned by a local educational agency and applies Housing Accountability Act protections to qualifying projects.
summaries.AB 1050: Lets certain housing projects redeveloping commercial property remove private covenants that restrict residential use, including reciprocal easement agreements. County counsel and recorder duties in the covenant modification process expand accordingly.
summaries.AB 1055: Would additionally authorize a local agency to require the property owner to certify, that the accessory dwelling unit will be occupied as a residential dwelling unit for at least 6 months out of each calendar year. Would authorize the local agency to annually recertify, that the accessory dwelling unit is occupied as a residential dwelling unit for at least 6 months out of each calendar year.
summaries.AB 1061: Expands ministerial housing and urban lot split eligibility in historic areas by focusing exclusions on contributing structures and individually listed historic resources. Local agencies may apply objective standards to preserve the historic district’s value.
summaries.AB 107: Changes state budget appropriations for fiscal years 2023–24 through 2025–26. The digest does not identify a specific LUS planning requirement.
summaries.AB 1089: Allows the Department of Fish and Wildlife to delegate western Joshua tree take authorization to cities for commercial and industrial projects under an agreement.
summaries.AB 11: Would enact the Social Housing Act and would create the California Housing Authority as an independent state body, the mission of which would be to ensure that social housing developments that are produced and acquired align with the goals of eliminating the gap between housing production and regional housing needs assessment targets and preserving affordable housing.
summaries.AB 1131: Would, for the 7th and each subsequent revision of the housing element, authorize a planning agency to include in that report the number of units approved for congregate care for the elderly, for up to 15% of a jurisdiction’s regional housing need allocation for any income category.
summaries.AB 1139: Extends a CEQA exemption for nonmotorized public access on existing park roads and trails to county park agencies, with revised resource management conditions before an exemption finding.
summaries.AB 1143: Would require, on or before January 1, 2027, the State Fire Marshal’s Wildfire Mitigation Advisory Committee to develop a home hardening certification program that identifies home hardening measures, including defensible space, that can be implemented during renovation or property improvement projects, or both, to substantially reduce the risk of loss during a fire and bring existing building stock into alignment with state building standards for wildland-urban interface areas.
summaries.AB 1154: Limits the owner occupancy requirement for a junior ADU to units sharing sanitation facilities with the existing home, and revises the rental provisions that local JADU ordinances must include.
summaries.AB 1156: Moves authority to waive or defer Williamson Act contract cancellation fees from a city or county to the Secretary of the Natural Resources Agency, including a route for qualifying photovoltaic solar facilities.
summaries.AB 1165: Would enact the California Housing Justice Act of 2026, which would require the department to create, by August 1, 2030, finance plans to solve homelessness and to solve the housing unaffordability crisis, and related statewide performance metrics. Would also require the department to seek public consult in developing those finance plans.
summaries.AB 1203: Would require the department and the Office of Community Partnerships and Strategic Communications to include, within the Save Our Water Campaign, a statewide “water wise” designation to be awarded to businesses in the CII sector that meet or exceed the recommendations for CII water use best management practices pursuant to those performance measures.
summaries.AB 1206: Would require each local agency, to develop a program for the preapproval of single-family and multifamily residential housing plans, whereby the local agency accepts single-family and multifamily plan submissions for preapproval and approves or denies the preapproval applications. Would require a large jurisdiction, to develop this program by July 1, 2026, and a small jurisdiction, to develop a program by January 1, 2028.
summaries.AB 1227: Requires CalEPA and the Natural Resources Agency to report to the Legislature on implementation of an emergency proclamation. The digest identifies no new local planning duty.
summaries.AB 1275: Moves the regional housing needs determination to three years before a scheduled housing element revision instead of two years and adjusts HCD consultation deadlines with councils of governments.
summaries.AB 1276: Would include in the definition of “ordinances, policies, and standards” materials requirements, postentitlement permit standards, and any rules, regulations, determinations, and other requirements adopted or implemented by other public agencies.
summaries.AB 1294: Creates a partial property tax welfare exemption from 2027 through 2029 for qualifying low and moderate income rental housing.
summaries.AB 130: Among its housing changes, bars fees and financial requirements in private ADU and JADU restrictions and revises local ministerial ADU approval rules. Review the full omnibus text before updating County standards.
summaries.AB 1308: Requires local building departments to inspect certain completed residential construction or additions within ten business days of receiving notice that permitted work is complete.
summaries.AB 1314: Would require all counties and program contracts to also ensure that decisions about sharing bedrooms, bathrooms, and units together are led by the program participant and agreed upon in collaboration with the provider.
summaries.AB 1407: Extends the deadline to complete required housing element rezoning after a late, noncompliant housing element from one year to 18 months after the statutory adoption deadline.
summaries.AB 1444: Would require any public notice that is legally required to be published in a newspaper of general circulation to be published in the newspaper’s print publication, on the newspaper’s internet website or electronic newspaper available on the internet, and on the statewide internet website maintained as a repository for notices by a majority of California newspapers of general circulation.
summaries.AB 145: Would subject a rezoning that would allow for the construction of a bed and breakfast inn, motel, hotel, or other transient lodging to CEQA review even if the rezoning implements a schedule of actions contained in an approved housing element. Would specify that other transient lodging does not include a residential hotel, or a resident’s use or marketing of a unit as short-term lodging, in a manner that is consistent with local law.
summaries.AB 1455: Directs the state board to adopt rules for the five foot ember resistant zone and other defensible space requirements in very high fire hazard severity zones designated by a local agency.
summaries.AB 1457: Would require a city, county, or city and county to meaningfully involve disadvantaged communities in the development, adoption, and implementation of the environmental justice element, or the related goals, policies, and objectives integrated in other elements, using methods that are designed to effectively involve disadvantaged communities based on local conditions and circumstances.
summaries.AB 1529: Allows tenant protection notices in a lease or rental agreement and changes notice procedures for assisted housing developments facing expiration of affordability restrictions or subsidy contracts.
summaries.AB 1553: Would authorize a lead agency to satisfy the direct mailing requirements listed above by electronic mail if the recipient affirmatively requested to receive notice by electronic mail.
summaries.AB 1567: Would, for the 7th and each subsequent revision of the housing element, authorize a planning agency to include in that report the number of units approved for congregate care for the elderly or residential care facilities for the elderly, for up to 15% of a jurisdiction’s regional housing need allocation for any income category, if congregate housing for the elderly or residential care facilities is included in the regional housing need determination.
summaries.AB 1573: Adds survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking to the groups that may be included in the housing element definition of target population for supportive housing.
summaries.AB 1577: For a discretionary data center permit, entitlement, or land use authorization, the owner or operator must give the permitting city or county estimates of annual energy use and operating sound levels. The local agency may use the information for land use and infrastructure planning, energy assessment, and environmental review. Separate operating reports go to the California Energy Commission.
summaries.AB 1600: Requires CalEPA to assess barriers farmworker communities face in accessing disadvantaged community investments, publish its findings, and develop an engagement strategy on environmental and health burdens.
summaries.AB 1621: Would prohibit a local agency or state agency from requiring or requesting more than 2 plan check and specification reviews in connection with an application for a building permit, as part of its review. Would authorize a local agency or state agency to deny an application that is not compliant with the permit standards following 2 plan check and specification reviews.
summaries.AB 1624: The measure, the Public Lands Protection Act, would, upon transfer to any private or nonfederal entity of a parcel of land located within the state that is owned by the United States government on or after January 1, 2025, and that has been designated in an adopted general plan or zoning ordinance as open space, public land, resource conservation, or an equivalent conservation-oriented designation, immediately subject that parcel to the zoning designation and associated state and local restrictions.
summaries.AB 1663: Would alternatively allow the agent of a property owner to submit the permit request and to satisfy other related requirements imposed on a property owner. Would delete the requirement for the permit request to include a signed attestation or certification.
summaries.AB 1693: Would establish a similar streamlined approval process for a local permit for a tenant improvement relating to a retailer. Would require a qualified professional certifier, or the applicant, as applicable, to prepare certain affidavits related to the tenant improvement under penalty of perjury.
summaries.AB 1710: Applies a reasonable person consistency test to Permit Streamlining Act reviews of housing developments and emergency shelters. Substantial evidence supporting a reasonable finding of consistency with an applicable plan or standard would establish conformity; transient lodging portions are excluded.
summaries.AB 1732: Extends the CEQA exemption for qualifying affordable housing projects to January 2037 and includes eligible public university or college housing projects.
summaries.AB 1738: Requires cities and counties to offer remote inspection requests for certain permitted work on one and two family homes beginning in 2028, with authority to set technical protocols and suspend use after willful misrepresentation.
summaries.AB 1751: Creates a ministerial approval path for qualifying townhome ownership projects under the Missing Middle Townhome Ownership Act, with objective planning standards and application requirements.
summaries.AB 1801: Requires 180 days’ public notice, access to related documents, and two public meetings before a local or other public agency approves construction or reuse of a building for private civil immigration custody.
summaries.AB 1808: Would additionally authorize the department to enter into an agreement with a city to delegate to the city the ability to authorize the taking of a western Joshua tree associated with developing commercial and industrial projects.
summaries.AB 1815: Prevents local governments from imposing factory built housing standards that exceed or differ from applicable mandatory California Building Standards Code requirements.
summaries.AB 1820: Caps local permit fees for Level 2 electric vehicle chargers at multifamily housing at reasonable service costs and a capacity based schedule, unless the locality documents higher costs. The limits begin in July 2027, or January 2028 in smaller jurisdictions.
summaries.AB 1821: Requires an agency to decide whether a public records request seeks disclosable records it holds and notify the requester within ten business days.
summaries.AB 1834: Extends a land use exception to qualifying tracts zoned for mixed use, including projects with residential units.
summaries.AB 1855: Would instead eliminate the condition that the public project be exclusively used by zero-emission trains or certified Tier 4 or cleaner rolling stock or locomotives, thereby expanding the scope of the exemption. Would require, for purposes of the exemption, the mainline rail of the project, instead of the whole project, to be located entirely within an existing right-of-way or existing highway right-of-way.
summaries.AB 1893: Would expand eligible activities under the local assistance grant program to include projects undertaken by a local governmental entity involving the acquisition or installation of mobile rigid dip tanks or similar mobile and permanent infrastructure that is capable of providing helicopter-accessible water supplies for firefighting response or suppression purposes in very high fire and high fire hazard severity zones.
summaries.AB 1895: Expands exempt surplus land to include parcels unsuitable for housing because of hazards such as unstable slopes, landslides, subsidence, or liquefaction.
summaries.AB 1914: Would require a city, county, or city and county, no later than January 1, 2033, to prepare and adopt a childcare plan or integrate a childcare plan into the next adoption of the city, county, or city and county’s general plan to address the childcare needs of the jurisdiction.
summaries.AB 1953: Would require both the Office of Emergency Services and the Office of Tourism to establish a public registration system. Would require the offices to adopt regulations to administer their respective public registration systems.
summaries.AB 1964: Would require the Office of the State Fire Marshal, on or before January 1, 2028, to develop home hardening standards. Would require the State Fire Marshal to, on or before January 1, 2030, compile a report concerning homes in moderate, high, and very high fire hazard severity zones in state and local responsibility areas.
summaries.AB 1976: Limits late local meetings or actions that would reconsider, delay, or prevent a pedestrian or bicycle safety project after it reaches 90 percent design or receives a construction contract.
summaries.AB 1997: Shortens the approval or denial deadline for certain housing developments to 30 days after certification of a qualifying environmental impact report.
summaries.AB 2002: Would establish the Regional Early Action Planning Fund in the State Treasury for the purpose of providing councils of governments, regional entities, and jurisdictions with one-time funding, including grants for planning activities, to enable those entities to meet the 7th and subsequent cycles of the regional housing need assessment. Would require the department to allocate funds, upon appropriation by the Legislature, from the Regional Early Action Planning Fund to each council of governments or regional entity responsible for allocating regional housing need that applies and qualifies for those moneys.
summaries.AB 2005: Would instead require the local agency to require an applicant to select one of 2 sets of owner-occupancy requirements.
summaries.AB 2057: Would prohibit state agencies and local governments from adopting or enforcing a rule, regulation, resolution, or ordinance that directly or indirectly results in prohibiting the use of gas appliances in residential or nonresidential buildings.
summaries.AB 2074: Requires major transit cities to designate at least one regional transit hub district by July 2027 and allow downtown housing development within the district.
summaries.AB 2102: Would, on or before January 1, 2028, and every 2 years thereafter, require the department or a local entity to conduct an assessment, of all undeveloped public lands for which it is primarily responsible for preventing and suppressing fires to ensure that the public land is not a severe fire hazard. Would require this assessment to be posted on the department’s and local entity’s internet website and would require a local entity conducting the assessment to submit its assessment to the department.
summaries.AB 2112: Would additionally require that expert advisory committee to include an expert in soil carbon sequestration. Would establish the Climate-smart Organics Management for Protecting Our Soil and Terrain (COMPOST) Act of 2026.
summaries.AB 2118: Bars local objective standards from prohibiting or limiting mixed use development in qualifying housing projects under the Affordable Housing and High Road Jobs Act. Eligible projects may combine housing with office, retail, restaurant, or other uses allowed by zoning.
summaries.AB 2127: Would prohibit a local agency from prohibiting an accessory dwelling unit in an area solely because the lots are served by private sewage disposal systems. Would prohibit a local health officer from withholding approval based on a minimum lot size requirement if the private sewage disposal system meets certain operating requirements established by the State Water Resources Control Board and the regional water quality control board for that lot size.
summaries.AB 2139: Adds qualifying City of Ontario land to the exempt surplus land category, with recorded covenants governing its disposal.
summaries.AB 2152: Would also authorize the Governor to certify an essential local fire station project for streamlining as an infrastructure project if the Governor ensures that the project meets applicable criteria, including, among others, that the applicant agrees to pay the costs of the trial court and the court of appeal in hearing and deciding any case challenging a lead agency’s action on the project, and the applicant agrees to pay the costs of preparing the record of proceedings for the project.
summaries.AB 2170: Requires environmental review of new or expanded industrial uses near sensitive receptors, with the lead agency choosing an EIR, negative declaration, or mitigated negative declaration under the bill’s criteria.
summaries.AB 2175: Directs the Public Utilities Commission to make logistics and manufacturing businesses eligible to aggregate meters under certain net energy metering tariffs.
summaries.AB 2181: Would prohibit land improved with an operating hotel or motel from being valued, for purposes of establishing, adjusting, or resetting ground rent under an existing lease, based on density bonuses, concessions or incentives, or waivers, unless those density increases are entitled and vested as of the valuation date. Would also prohibit its provisions from being construed to alter the requirements for obtaining a density bonus.
summaries.AB 2182: Changes state financing rules for custom energy efficiency projects in agricultural and industrial facilities. The digest identifies no direct County land use approval duty.
summaries.AB 2239: Requires the Public Utilities Commission to enforce electrical utility energization timelines and impose penalties for missed targets.
summaries.AB 2288: Excludes adaptive reuse of sites with existing high hazard Group H occupancy from the streamlined adaptive reuse process.
summaries.AB 2295: Would authorize a local government, to enter into a voluntary agreement with another local government to allow new housing development projects to count toward each locality’s share of the regional housing needs allocation if applicable criteria are met, including that the project includes affordable housing units for very low and lower income households.
summaries.AB 2296: Changes housing element update timing for local governments in certain metropolitan and regional transportation planning areas to 18 months after every second regional transportation plan update.
summaries.AB 2320: Directs HCD to consider Homekey funding for adaptive reuse projects involving substantial rehabilitation, reconstruction, or demolition of an existing structure.
summaries.AB 2323: Would require any public notice that is legally required to be published in a newspaper of general circulation to be published in the newspaper’s print publication and on the newspaper’s internet website or electronic newspaper available on the internet.
summaries.AB 2351: Adds counts of temporary emergency shelter beds and permanent housing units serving people experiencing or leaving homelessness to annual planning agency reports beginning in 2028.
summaries.AB 2383: Would require, as part of a new or existing proceeding, the commission to require each electrical corporation to file a transmission and distribution service tariff and a generation service tariff for participating customers, that meet applicable criteria. Would also require, on or before January 1, 2028, each community choice aggregator or electric service provider to adopt a tariff for generation service for data centers, consistent with applicable criteria.
summaries.AB 2390: Would instead require the local government to approve a modification if it determines the modification is consistent with objective zoning standards, objective subdivision standards, and objective design review standards that were in effect when the original development application or notice of intent was first submitted, as described. Would also require subsequent modifications to be evaluated for consistency using the same assumptions and analytical methodology the local government originally used, or that was used in a previous modification, as described.
summaries.AB 2400: Would additionally require the city or county to include in the annual report the number of suite-style student housing quarters, as determined by the department.
summaries.AB 2415: Would provide that a transit-oriented development alternative plan may reduce the capacity in up to one transit-oriented development zone in total units or residential floor area by more than 50% if applicable criteria are met.
summaries.AB 2418: Revises private plan check rules for nonresidential building permits through 2031, including a requirement to give applicants an estimated review timeframe when an application is complete.
summaries.AB 2433: Revises when local governments must grant density bonuses, incentives, concessions, and waivers for qualifying housing applications.
summaries.AB 2469: Would prohibit a city, county, or city and county from approving a discretionary or ministerial permit or other entitlement that would result in the construction, or an expansion that increases the maximum peak water use, of a data center unless applicable criteria are satisfied, including, among others, that the applicant provides the city, county, or city and county prescribed information.
summaries.AB 2480: Provides an additional density bonus for eligible student housing developments and coordinates amendments with other density bonus bills.
summaries.AB 2517: Requires the State Fire Marshal to publish proposed local fire hazard severity zone designations and notify local governments at least 180 days before finalizing them.
summaries.AB 253: The measure, the California Residential Private Permitting Review Act, would require a county or city to prepare a residential building permit fee schedule and post the schedule on the county’s or city’s internet website, if the county or city prescribes residential building permit fees.
summaries.AB 2552: Would authorize a lead agency for a land use project to require an applicant to contribute to the Transit-Oriented Development Implementation Fund if certain cost conditions are met and the department and the office have validated the reductions in vehicle miles traveled that are attributable to the project.
summaries.AB 2569: Requires CEQA environmental impact reports to discuss significant effects of placing projects near, or attracting people to, existing or foreseeable natural hazards and adverse environmental conditions.
summaries.AB 2601: Lets a two unit housing application in a single family zone be processed concurrently with an urban lot split parcel map application.
summaries.AB 261: Would prohibit the State Fire Marshal’s determination of fire hazard severity zone, in both state responsibility areas and lands that are not state responsibility areas, from being based on risk mitigation activities. Would authorize the State Fire Marshal to provide a written response to an entity on actions that may impact the degree of fire hazard, and would require this written response to be posted on the State Fire Marshal’s internet website.
summaries.AB 2619: Would require a person who owns or operates a data center, prior to applying to a city or a county for an initial business license, equivalent instrument, or permit, to provide its water supplier, under penalty of perjury, a good faith estimate of the expected water use, the anticipated source of water, and the data center’s projected water use volume for the maximum day, maximum month, and average year.
summaries.AB 2620: Would exempt from CEQA projects for the installation of a wireless telecommunications facility, or a broadband internet access project, that is not a small wireless facility.
summaries.AB 2676: Expands the Housing Crisis Act restriction on local policies or standards that operate as a housing development moratorium.
summaries.AB 2689: Would specify, for housing projects where the low-income housing commitment requires 100% of the units, not including any manager’s units, to be restricted to lower income households, that good cause for nonrenewal of a lease includes cases where the nonrenewal relates to a household whose income exceeds 140% of the area median income for at least 2 consecutive years and 30% of the household’s monthly income exceeds the fair market rent, determined.
summaries.AB 2702: Would enact the Residential Care Facilities for the Elderly on Faith-Based Lands Act of 2026. Would require, notwithstanding any inconsistent provision of a local government’s general plan, specific plan, zoning ordinance, or regulation, that a residential care facility development project located on land owned by a religious institution be an allowable use at certain densities, if the development project satisfies all of the prescribed criteria.
summaries.AB 2741: Clarifies that local zoning for multifamily housing sites can use overlay, mixed use, or combining districts if both owner occupied and rental multifamily uses are allowed.
summaries.AB 2748: Allows affordable housing developments with permit applications submitted from January 2025 through December 2028 to meet electric vehicle charging receptacle requirements under either the 2025 California Green Building Standards Code or the 2024 supplement to the 2022 code. Local building departments enforce the applicable standard.
summaries.AB 282: Makes it a felony to seize ballots, election records, or certified voting technology before election results are certified. The digest identifies no land use or Planning duty.
summaries.AB 300: Would instead require the State Fire Marshal, at least once every 5 years, to review areas in the state identified as moderate, high, and very high fire hazard severity zones, and to review lands within state responsibility areas classified as fire hazard severity zones. Would also require the State Fire Marshal, at least once every 5 years, to re-review areas within the state that are not identified as moderate, high, and very high fire hazard severity zones, and to re-review lands within state responsibility areas that are not classified as fire hazard severity zones, and, if applicable, identify or classify those areas.
summaries.AB 301: Extends postentitlement permit transparency and processing rules to state agencies, including public lists of required application materials and examples of complete applications.
summaries.AB 306: Expands appeals to the California Building Standards Commission to cover requests for alternative building materials and revises how the commission reviews those appeals.
summaries.AB 36: Moves HCD prohousing designations to permanent regulations and provides consultation to qualifying small rural jurisdictions for the seventh housing element cycle.
summaries.AB 368: Would require the commission to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of passive house energy efficiency standards by California climate zone, using commission-adopted metrics such as long-term system cost. Would require the commission to evaluate the use of the 2 passive house energy models currently required for passive house certification in its analysis and the cost-effectiveness of passive house construction compared to existing construction.
summaries.AB 385: Allows San Bernardino County to dispose of up to 4.2 acres at Glen Helen Regional Park if it acquires replacement park property of equal or greater recreational value.
summaries.AB 39: Requires local governments to prepare a local electrification plan, or integrate one into a general plan update, between 2027 and 2030.
summaries.AB 431: Adds advanced air mobility to the next California Transportation Plan update and creates a state working group on related infrastructure.
summaries.AB 436: The measure, on or before June 1, 2027, would require the Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation, in consultation with the Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery, to develop and post on the office’s internet website, a technical advisory, reflecting best practices to facilitate the siting of composting facilities to meet the organic waste reduction goals.
summaries.AB 462: The measure, notwithstanding that prohibition, would require a local agency to issue a certificate of occupancy for an accessory dwelling unit constructed in a county that is subject to a proclamation of a state of emergency made by the Governor on or after February 1, 2025, even if the primary dwelling has not yet been issued a certificate of occupancy, if applicable criteria are met, including that the primary dwelling was substantially damaged or destroyed by an event referenced in the state of emergency proclamation.
summaries.AB 474: Expands an owner occupied single family home rental exception under fair housing law for certain roomers or boarders sharing the household.
summaries.AB 507: Allows qualifying adaptive reuse projects by right in any zone through streamlined ministerial review, subject to the bill’s eligibility and safety limits.
summaries.AB 518: Would specify that, for purposes of that act, a special occupancy park does not include a low-impact camping area, that is located in a county that has enacted an ordinance, authorizing low-impact camping and meeting applicable criteria. Would impose applicable criteria on owners of private property offering low-impact camping area sites and on online hosting platforms.
summaries.AB 527: Expands geothermal exploratory project rules to include equipment and work connecting wells and reservoirs, and revises which wells count toward a distance limit.
summaries.AB 531: Would expand the types of facilities eligible to be certified as environmental leadership development projects by the Energy Commission to include geothermal powerplants and projects that comprise multiple geothermal powerplants on a single site.
summaries.AB 534: Would require a contract for a transitional housing placement provider or a Transitional Housing Program-Plus provider to have an initial term of 3 years. Would authorize a contract to be renewed for 2 additional 1-year terms.
summaries.AB 550: Would also allow the department to authorize by permit the take of a species proposed for listing, if applicable criteria are met. Would require the department to, on or before January 31, 2033, compile and post a summary table on its internet website with information for calendar years 2027 to 2032, inclusive.
summaries.AB 557: Allows approved factory built housing plans to be reused by unit serial number on later projects unless applicable building standards change.
summaries.AB 580: Extends through January 2041 the special surface mining master reclamation plan and environmental review provisions for Metropolitan Water District of Southern California operations.
summaries.AB 592: Changes retail food and catering authorization rules, including ending new COVID-19 temporary catering authorizations in 2027. The digest identifies no direct LUS planning duty.
summaries.AB 609: Creates a CEQA exemption for qualifying housing developments based on size, density, and location, with additional conditions for housing within 500 feet of a freeway.
summaries.AB 610: Requires the seventh and later housing elements to disclose new or tightened governmental constraints adopted since the prior element deadline, alongside the existing analysis of barriers to housing.
summaries.AB 630: The measure, until January 1, 2030, would authorize the Counties of Alameda and Los Angeles to implement similar procedures for the disposal of recreational vehicles, valued at $4,000 or less. Would impose applicable criteria on this authority, including requiring a public agency, prior to disposing of a recreational vehicle, to provide authorization that the recreational vehicle is inoperable.
summaries.AB 632: Lets local agencies record a final administrative fine or penalty order with the superior court clerk for enforcement under the bill’s process.
summaries.AB 648: Would provide that a community college district is not required to comply with the zoning ordinances of a city, county, or city and county, for a university housing development project constructed on property owned or leased by a community college district if specific requirements are met. If the project includes units for faculty and staff, the bill would require the community college district to ensure that a portion of the units of the project are made available at affordable rents to extremely low income faculty and staff and lower income faculty and staff.
summaries.AB 650: Requires HCD to develop a standardized housing element reporting format by the end of 2026 and moves regional housing need determinations from two to three years before scheduled housing element revisions.
summaries.AB 66: Would, until January 1, 2032, exempt from CEQA egress route projects undertaken by a public agency to improve emergency access to and evacuation from a subdivision without a secondary egress route if the State Board of Forestry and Fire Protection has recommended the creation of a secondary access to the subdivision and applicable criteria are met. Would require the lead agency to hold a noticed public meeting to hear and respond to public comments before determining that a project is exempt.
summaries.AB 660: Would prohibit the local agency from requiring or requesting more than 2 plan check and specification reviews in connection with an application for a building permit, as part of its review, except. Would authorize a local agency to deny an application that is not compliant with the permit standards following 2 plan check and specification reviews.
summaries.AB 670: Would, beginning with the report due by April 1, 2027, require information to be included in the report, including additional information regarding units of new housing, the units of housing demolished, and a report on replacement housing units.
summaries.AB 671: Would establish a streamlined approval process for a local permit for a tenant improvement, relating to a restaurant. In this regard, the bill would require a local building department, upon the request and at the expense of the permit applicant, to allow a qualified professional certifier, defined as a licensed architect or engineer who meets applicable criteria, to certify that the plans and specifications of the tenant improvement comply with all applicable building, health, and safety codes.
summaries.AB 678: Directs the state homelessness council to consult LGBTQ+ communities on inclusive services and recommend practices for people experiencing homelessness.
summaries.AB 687: Would additionally require that coverage if the screening test is approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration and either meets requirements for coverage established by the federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, or is included in the most recently published guidelines from the American Cancer Society.
summaries.AB 712: Would extend any period of limitation for actions under any state law for a period of 60 days beginning on the date the applicant provides written notice to the local agency indicating its intent to commence an action. Would prohibit a public agency from requiring the applicant to indemnify, defend, or hold harmless the public agency in any action alleging the public agency violated the applicant’s rights or deprived the applicant of the benefits or protection provide by a housing reform law.
summaries.AB 722: Establishes a state reentry housing and workforce development grant program for people leaving incarceration, subject to legislative funding.
summaries.AB 726: Allows a city or county to report qualifying substantially rehabilitated, older deed restricted affordable units in its annual housing report, while excluding those units from streamlined approval affordability calculations.
summaries.AB 735: Would clarify that a 21st century warehouse and a tier 1 21st century warehouse are required to comply with those standards as are in effect at the time that the building permit for a development of a 21st century warehouse is issued and make other clarifying changes relating to permissibility of use of conduits and electrical hookups at loading bays at those locations.
summaries.AB 736: Would, beginning January 1, 2027, prohibit a local jurisdiction, defined to include a city, including a charter city, county, or city and county, from collecting a transfer tax, levied on the sale or transfer of a real property interest conveyed if the combined transfer tax rate levied by the local jurisdiction exceeds 1.5% of the consideration paid for or value of the real property interest conveyed, except as otherwise provided.
summaries.AB 738: Would, until January 1, 2028, require residential construction intended to repair, restore, or replace a residential building damaged or destroyed as a result of a disaster in an area in which a state of emergency has been proclaimed by the Governor to comply only with the requirements regarding photovoltaic systems pursuant to those regulations, if any, that were in effect at the time the damaged or destroyed building was originally constructed and would prohibit that construction from being required to comply with any additional or conflicting photovoltaic system requirements in effect at the time of repair, restoration, or replacement.
summaries.AB 745: Temporarily permits certain excess tax school districts to seek reorganization through a state approval process. The digest identifies no direct LUS planning requirement.
summaries.AB 748: Would require each local agency, to develop a program for the preapproval of single-family and multifamily residential housing plans, whereby the local agency accepts single-family and multifamily plan submissions for preapproval and approves or denies the preapproval applications. Would require a large jurisdiction, to develop this program by July 1, 2027, and a small jurisdiction, to develop a program by January 1, 2029.
summaries.AB 750: Would also authorize the department to make those loans and grants to rehabilitate, capitalize operating subsidy reserves for, and extend the long-term affordability of housing projects that qualify as a challenged development. Would require the department to grant priority for these loans and grants to housing projects that are department funded and have an affordability restriction that has expired or have a remaining term of less than 10 years, or are otherwise at risk for conversion.
summaries.AB 752: Would similarly require a daycare center, when colocated with multifamily housing, to be considered a residential use of property and a use by right. Would similarly prohibit a local jurisdiction from imposing a charge, tax, or fee for a business license, equivalent instrument, or permit for the privilege of operating a daycare center that is colocated with multifamily housing.
summaries.AB 76: Changes an exempt surplus land provision for a defined sectional planning area and sets a minimum share of housing units outside academic institution housing.
summaries.AB 782: Narrows the commercial property redevelopment housing rule by excluding certain projects in charter cities that meet the bill’s criteria.
summaries.AB 803: Adds school greening and tree shaded school grounds to the state urban forestry program’s benefits, technical assistance, and grant purposes; it also extends the state strategic plan deadline.
summaries.AB 804: Makes housing support services for eligible Medi Cal members a covered benefit if the Legislature funds them. The digest identifies no direct LUS planning requirement.
summaries.AB 806: Invalidates certain rental agreement or governing document restrictions on mobilehome residents and homeowners under the bill’s housing rules.
summaries.AB 818: Requires local governments to approve or deny a complete building permit application within ten business days for certain temporary structures used after a disaster.
summaries.AB 823: Would, on and after January 1, 2029, prohibit a person from selling, offering for sale, distributing, or offering for promotional purposes in this state a personal care product containing plastic glitter, or a personal care product in a non-rinse-off product or a cleaning product containing one ppm or more by weight of plastic microbeads that are used as an abrasive.
summaries.AB 839: Allows the Governor to certify up to three sustainable aviation fuel projects for expedited CEQA judicial review as infrastructure projects.
summaries.AB 846: Would authorize a city, county, city and county, special district, or other local agency to submit to the department a wildfire preparedness plan to conduct wildfire preparedness activities on land designated as a fire hazard severity zone, that minimizes impacts to wildlife and habitat for candidate, threatened, and endangered species.
summaries.AB 864: Requires state workshops by July 2028 on how federal hazardous waste rules apply to streams including solar photovoltaic modules.
summaries.AB 87: Would specify that certain provisions of the Density Bonus Law do not require a city, county, or city and county to approve, grant a concession or incentive requiring approval of, or waive or reduce development standards otherwise applicable to, transient lodging as part of a housing development.
summaries.AB 888: Creates a state Safe Homes grant program to help reduce wildfire losses, with priorities for awarding grants.
summaries.AB 893: Would provide that, for purposes of determining whether a property or site satisfies the criteria, objective development standards, or other requirements for receiving streamlined, ministerial review under the act, a local government’s review of the property or site is limited to the area described as being physically disturbed by construction in the application for streamlined, ministerial review and does not include, unless expressly stated otherwise, other contiguous or noncontiguous areas even if under the ownership or control of the project proponent.
summaries.AB 902: Would require a lead agency to incorporate appropriate wildlife passage features into a transportation infrastructure project in a connectivity area. Would exempt a project on the state highway system from this requirement if Caltrans is the lead agency.
summaries.AB 906: Would remove the requirement on cities and counties to include the 2nd analysis in their housing elements.
summaries.AB 920: Requires cities and counties with at least 150,000 residents to provide a central online portal for housing development applications.
summaries.AB 93: Would require a person who owns or operates a data center, prior to applying to a city or a county for an initial business license, equivalent instrument, or permit, to provide its water supplier, under penalty of perjury, an estimate of the expected water use. When applying to a city or county for an initial business license, the bill would require a person who owns or operates a data center to self-certify, under penalty of perjury, on the application that the person has provided its water supplier an estimate of the expected water use.
summaries.AB 939: Allows a nonprofit housing corporation to purchase certain for sale affordable units to satisfy housing development affordability requirements.
summaries.AB 945: Would require a city or county to grant additional incentives or concessions when an applicant proposes to construct a green housing development. Would require that the number of incentives or concessions granted initially be set to 3 and would require HCD, to evaluate and report on the number and type of units and developments entitled, permitted, and constructed pursuant to these provisions.
summaries.AB 946: Would provide that, to advance and promote environmental, conservation, and public access policies and budget actions, the Governor’s office, state agencies, and the Legislature, when distributing resources, shall recognize the coequal goals and benefits of the 30x30 goal and the Outdoors for All initiative, and, to the extent practical, maximize investment in historically underserved urban communities consistent with those initiatives.
summaries.AB 956: Would revise the provision governing prohibitions or restrictions on the construction or use of an accessory dwelling unit or junior accessory dwelling unit on a lot zoned for single-family residential use to instead apply to a lot zoned to allow single-family residential use.
summaries.AB 982: Allows certain idle construction aggregate mines to request a temporary Idle Reserve Mine Status through 2032, with state review and reclamation requirements.
summaries.SB 1003: Would authorize a city or county that is designated as prohousing to establish a prohousing enhanced infrastructure financing district if applicable criteria are met. Would prescribe requirements applicable to those districts.
summaries.SB 1008: Exempts a Public Utilities Commission ordered closure of a railroad grade crossing that poses a public safety threat from CEQA, except high speed rail crossings. The lead agency must file a notice of exemption.
summaries.SB 1014: Lets housing applicants request an early estimate of required public improvements when submitting a preliminary or full project application.
summaries.SB 1036: Would require the amount of a fee that is imposed on a development project that demolishes or changes an existing use to be offset to account for the demolition or change so that the amount of the fee is attributable only to the development project’s incremental impact on public facilities or services.
summaries.SB 1061: Would authorize the department to authorize, by permit, and without payment of fees or other mitigation, the relocation of up to 10 individual western Joshua trees from a parcel. Would require a person seeking a relocation permit to submit a permit application to the department and meet applicable criteria including, among other conditions, that the tree identified in the application would be relocated within 2.5 kilometers of its original location and that the relocation be consistent with the guidelines and relocation protocols adopted by the department.
summaries.SB 1062: Would require the department to consider making the fees proportionate to the impact of a project and the use of tiered fees by project type, size, or other criteria.
summaries.SB 1063: Would authorize the department to permit the taking of a western Joshua tree without payment of fees or other mitigation upon demonstration to the department that the taking of a western Joshua tree is related to the maintenance, operation, or construction of a life-sustaining service connection to a single-family residence or multifamily residence, including distribution infrastructure.
summaries.SB 107: Would amend those budget acts by amending, adding, and repealing items of appropriation and making other changes.
summaries.SB 1072: Changes several housing laws, including Housing Accountability Act litigation deadlines and notice to public entities when assisted housing restrictions or subsidies end. Review the omnibus provisions that affect County housing workflows.
summaries.SB 1085: Requires a city or county to identify potential public water suppliers early in certain housing applications and request a water demand determination within 15 days. For qualifying projects, water systems must return assessments within 45 rather than 90 days.
summaries.SB 1116: Measures qualifying housing height limits by a building’s physical height rather than floor count and restricts certain local setbacks.
summaries.SB 1117: Would require the charge for certain accessory dwelling units to be based only on the area in excess of 750 square feet of interior livable space.
summaries.SB 1154: Allows community college districts to use best value procurement for public projects over $1 million through 2030.
summaries.SB 1168: Would require the commission to assess opportunities for rate structures to ensure data centers pay a reasonable share of their costs associated with transmission and distribution needs, ensure that data centers pay for their proportionate share of load increases and procurements needed to reliably serve their loads while maintaining consistency with the applicable integrated resource planning requirements, and alleviate cost pressures on residential ratepayers.
summaries.SB 1169: Would extend the initial expiration period of an approved or conditionally approved tentative map to 48 months and the extension pursuant to local ordinance to 36 months.
summaries.SB 1182: Adds insurance availability for existing and planned uses in high wildfire hazard areas to safety elements updated from 2028 onward.
summaries.SB 1196: Would require the commission, by September 30, 2027, in a new or existing proceeding, to establish timelines for electrical corporations to respond to and process requests to energize small energization projects. Would require the commission, in establishing the timelines for energization, to require electrical corporations to comply with applicable criteria.
summaries.SB 1213: Changes eligibility rules for medium and heavy duty vehicles under the state clean truck and bus technology program.
summaries.SB 1216: Amends a 2026 state budget appropriation. The digest identifies no direct LUS planning requirement.
summaries.SB 1241: Expands public contract notice and disclosure requirements to include development agreements and resolutions.
summaries.SB 1256: Would prohibit an action or proceeding to enforce the Subdivision Map Act from being maintained if certain criteria exist, including that the action or proceeding to enforce the Subdivision Map Act includes substantially similar claims or issues to claims or issues raised in an action or proceeding to enforce CEQA and the defendant in the action or proceeding to enforce the Subdivision Map Act was the defendant in the action or proceeding to enforce CEQA.
summaries.SB 1258: Would require the State Water Resources Control Board, working jointly with the department and in consultation with the Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation, to develop guidelines for developers and for agencies overseeing development-specific site remediations and making determinations of site suitability. Would require the board, in conjunction with the department, to develop thresholds of significance for contaminants from different sources and for different future uses.
summaries.SB 1272: Requires more time to correct nonemergency building, plumbing, electrical, or zoning violations before local enforcement under qualifying circumstances.
summaries.SB 1283: Would require this administrative approval to extend to EV stations with a canopy, or onsite energy storage systems sized to support charging. Would also require any electric vehicle supply equipment installed at the EV station to meet all applicable safety and performance standards.
summaries.SB 130: Bars fees and other financial requirements in otherwise reasonable private restrictions on constructing or using ADUs and JADUs.
summaries.SB 1317: Adds qualifying local surplus land within a property and business improvement district to the exempt surplus land definition.
summaries.SB 1326: Expands the definition of tribal cultural resource to include places and objects identified by a California Native American tribe as culturally valuable, affecting CEQA resource review.
summaries.SB 1350: Adds qualifying hydrogen fueled turbine facilities to the definition of renewable electrical generation facilities.
summaries.SB 1361: Restricts actions by local governments near planned or existing transit oriented development stops that could interfere with transit agencies or projects.
summaries.SB 1367: Restricts city and county land use approvals for new or converted detention facilities under the bill’s definition.
summaries.SB 1375: Exempts qualifying urban intermodal rail station projects where light, commuter, and intercity rail converge from CEQA.
summaries.SB 1383: Revises density bonus concessions for buildings over 85 feet, including how development standard reductions and zoning changes are treated.
summaries.SB 1414: Creates an independent citizens commission to redraw San Bernardino County Board of Supervisors district boundaries, subject to state funding. The digest identifies no direct LUS planning duty.
summaries.SB 1423: Requires the state to publish standardized spatial planning datasets through a consolidated online platform by July 2028.
summaries.SB 1426: Reorganizes the Planning and Zoning Law’s local annual report provisions without a substantive change to the reported information, according to the Legislative Counsel digest.
summaries.SB 1439: Defines terms used in local government advisory body and program rules and makes other omnibus changes. Review the full text for any County operational effect.
summaries.SB 158: Makes multiple land use and housing changes, including reducing the maximum builder’s remedy site size for a CEQA exemption from five to four acres and requiring a notice of exemption to the state planning office and county clerk. Review the full budget trailer bill for other County provisions.
summaries.SB 16: Requires county behavioral health directors to establish training and designation procedures for professionals who perform involuntary mental health evaluations. The digest identifies no LUS planning duty.
summaries.SB 21: Counts replacement protected housing units when determining whether a development meets certain affordability requirements.
summaries.SB 222: Limits local permits, inspections, fees, and additional planning standards for residential heat pump water heaters and HVAC replacements beginning July 2027. Qualifying plug in window units cannot be required to obtain a local permit or inspection.
summaries.SB 233: Moves state consultation with regional councils of governments earlier in the housing needs determination process for the seventh and later housing element cycles.
summaries.SB 262: Broadens the state definition of prohousing local policies to include policies that help residents remain housed.
summaries.SB 282: Would require a city, county, or city and county to adopt and offer asynchronous inspections for installations of residential heat pump water heater or heat pump HVAC systems, that do not require a licensed contractor and building inspector to be simultaneously present during the inspection.
summaries.SB 283: Requires energy storage applicants to certify that they consulted the local fire suppression authority at least 30 days before applying. Operations cannot begin before that authority inspects the completed system.
summaries.SB 299: Would exempt from CEQA a project that consists exclusively of a day care center, that is located in a residential area.
summaries.SB 326: Would require the deputy director, on or before January 1, 2027, and every 3 years thereafter, in consultation with the state hazard mitigation officer, to prepare a Wildfire Risk Mitigation Planning Framework sufficient to quantitatively evaluate wildfire risk mitigation actions. Would require the framework to allow for geospatial evaluation and comparison of wildfire risk mitigation actions, as described, sufficient to direct coordinated mitigation efforts and long-term collaborative mitigation planning.
summaries.SB 340: Would additionally require an emergency shelter to include all services provided onsite, including the addition or expansion of services that are consistent with certain written, objective standards.
summaries.SB 346: Would authorize a local agency, defined to mean a city, county, or city and county, to enact an ordinance to require a short-term rental facilitator, to report, in the form and manner prescribed by the local agency, the physical address, including 9-digit ZIP Code, of each short-term rental, during the reporting period. Would also authorize a local agency to request additional information, when the physical address is not sufficient for the local agency to identify a specific short-term rental.
summaries.SB 358: Would require those findings to be supported by substantial evidence in the record before or as part of the housing development project approval process.
summaries.SB 415: Would clarify that a 21st century warehouse and a tier 1 21st century warehouse are required to comply with those standards as are in effect at the time that the building permit for a development of a 21st century warehouse is issued and make other clarifying changes relating to permissibility of use of conduits and electrical hookups at loading bays at those locations.
summaries.SB 417: Would enact the Veterans and Affordable Housing Bond Act of 2026, which, if adopted, would authorize the issuance of bonds in the amount of $11,250,000,000, pursuant to the State General Obligation Bond Law.
summaries.SB 429: Creates a state wildfire risk modeling and grant program, subject to legislative funding.
summaries.SB 445: Would require the authority, on or before July 1, 2026, to develop and adopt internal rules, setting forth standards and timelines for the authority to engage utilities to ensure coordination and cooperation in relocating utility infrastructure or otherwise resolving utility conflicts affecting the delivery of the high-speed rail project.
summaries.SB 457: Directs HCD to provide formulas for realistic housing element site capacity by July 2028. Local inventories must show units allowed on each site before and after rezoning, and jurisdictions may use the state formula.
summaries.SB 486: Would require the sustainable communities strategy, in identifying areas within the region sufficient to house all the population of the region, to also take into account changes in enrollment levels at institutions of public higher education.
summaries.SB 489: Requires each local agency formation commission to adopt written policies, procedures, and forms for complete applications.
summaries.SB 492: Would require the department, on or before July 1, 2029, in consultation with the Department of Insurance, the Natural Resources Agency, the Office of Emergency Services, and other relevant departments, to develop standards for state and local agencies to aggregate and make available data related to parcel-, neighborhood-, and community-level wildfire risk for the purpose of enabling a wildfire data sharing platform.
summaries.SB 499: Allows local agencies to collect utility connection service charges when an application is received.
summaries.SB 5: Excludes taxes on Williamson Act and farmland security zone parcels from certain district or authority tax allocations.
summaries.SB 507: Lets a local government make a voluntary agreement with a tribe in the same county to count new tribal housing toward the jurisdiction’s regional housing need allocation.
summaries.SB 514: Extends the state defensible space and home hardening assessment program indefinitely and lets qualified nonprofit entities assess local responsibility areas. It limits use of voluntarily provided property data for enforcement.
summaries.SB 526: Expands state affiliate clinic licensing and relocation options for eligible primary care clinic corporations. The digest identifies no direct LUS planning requirement.
summaries.SB 543: Would revise the definition of a “junior accessory dwelling unit” to require the size of a JADU to be no more than 500 square feet of interior livable space.
summaries.SB 606: Changes Homeless Housing, Assistance, and Prevention planning and applications by introducing a functional zero goal for homelessness programs.
summaries.SB 611: Restores a CEQA review process for qualifying community plan updates adopted since 2025 and development applications completed by the local jurisdiction by January 2036.
summaries.SB 616: Requires a joint powers authority to consider updating its wildfire mitigation program using community hardening standards.
summaries.SB 625: Makes private covenants or governing documents void to the extent they prohibit or unreasonably restrict qualifying housing development under the bill’s rule.
summaries.SB 629: Would require the factors on which the fire severity zones are based to include areas within the perimeter of a wildfire that burned 1,000 or more acres, destroyed more than 10 structures, or resulted in a fatality, and to include areas at risk for an urban conflagration that accounts for the potential for structures to serve as a fuel source that extends the ember cast outside of wildland areas and areas where agricultural land affects fire hazard.
summaries.SB 635: Would prohibit a local authority, except as otherwise required by state or federal law, from providing voluntary consent to any individual to access, review, or obtain certain records of the local authority that include personally identifiable information of any sidewalk vendors in the jurisdiction without a subpoena or judicial warrant. Would also prohibit a local authority and its personnel from disclosing or providing in writing, verbally, or in any other manner personally identifiable information of any sidewalk vendor that is requested, except pursuant to a subpoena or a valid judicial warrant.
summaries.SB 653: Defines environmentally sensitive vegetation management that reduces wildfire risk while supporting native habitat, and changes state public entity project procedures.
summaries.SB 655: Would declare it to be the established policy of the state that all dwelling units, are required to be able to attain and maintain a safe maximum indoor temperature. Would require all relevant state agencies to consider this state policy when revising, adopting, or establishing policies, programs, and criteria, including grant criteria, that are relevant to achieving the state policy and, beginning January 1, 2027, when revising, adopting, or establishing regulations that are relevant to achieving this state policy.
summaries.SB 677: Would provide that the geographic jurisdiction of a joint powers authority is the area encompassed by the combined geographical boundaries of all of its member public agencies.
summaries.SB 681: Bars fees and other financial requirements in private restrictions on constructing or using ADUs and JADUs, and limits certain landlord charges.
summaries.SB 71: Extends transit project CEQA exemptions and adds certain transit route analyses and changes, with exceptions for ferry terminals and transportation network company services.
summaries.SB 715: Moves several state election notification deadlines earlier. The digest identifies no direct LUS planning requirement.
summaries.SB 722: Would additionally prohibit the development from being located on an existing parcel of land or site governed under the Mobilehome Residency Law, the Recreational Vehicle Park Occupancy Law, the Mobilehome Parks Act, or the Special Occupancy Parks Act.
summaries.SB 748: Would, as part of this description, additionally require the applicant to include information about safe parking sites, when the application includes operating safe parking sites while locating interim or permanent housing for people experiencing homelessness living in vehicles or recreational vehicles.
summaries.SB 757: Allows cities and counties through 2034 to collect qualifying nuisance abatement fines by lien or special assessment.
summaries.SB 786: Applies the general plan validity challenge process to charter cities and limits certain court continuances.
summaries.SB 79: Allows qualifying housing development near transit oriented development stops on residential, mixed use, and commercial sites, subject to the law’s transit distance and eligibility rules.
summaries.SB 815: Requires local safety elements to include a wildfire retrofit strategy, with periodic review, and land use elements in jurisdictions with homes in very high fire hazard areas to identify those areas and protective measures.
summaries.SB 838: Would revise the definition of “housing development project” to, in the case of mixed-use developments with at least 2/3 of the new or converted square footage designated for residential use, require that no portion of the project be designated for use as a hotel, motel, bed and breakfast inn, or other transient lodging.
summaries.SB 866: Expands a homelessness program report to include allocated government funding and outreach to unhoused people.
summaries.SB 887: Would define “data center” for the purposes of CEQA and prohibit the application of categorical exemption to a project for the development and operation of a data center.
summaries.SB 9: Invalidates a local urban lot split ordinance if the agency does not send it to HCD within 60 days or respond to HCD’s noncompliance findings within 30 days.
summaries.SB 908: Would declare void and unenforceable any covenant, restriction, or condition contained in any deed, contract, security instrument, other instrument affecting the transfer or sale of any interest in a common interest development, or provision of a governing document that effectively prohibits or restricts the owner of a separate interest from completing a residential window replacement project or impose any requirements on California Energy Code-compliant windows.
summaries.SB 92: Limits how Density Bonus Law concessions affect commercial floor area ratios and clarifies that transient lodging does not receive certain housing concessions.
summaries.SB 924: Would require the commission to take into consideration the cost-effectiveness of the services as a whole and to require electrical corporations and gas corporations, in performing those home weatherization services, to prioritize integration of health, safety, and indoor air quality improvement measures necessary to enable whole-home improvements, coordinated delivery across fuel types and housing types, conditions, and tenancy structures, and program design that allows for tenant-level benefits where upgrades occur in rental properties, while preserving flexibility in program design.
summaries.SB 954: Would revise the definition of that term to include habitats for protected species identified as candidate, sensitive, or species of special status by state or federal agencies.
summaries.SB 958: Would, for purposes of CEQA, prohibit the environmental impacts that are associated with increased building height alone from being considered significant impacts on the environment, if a project meets applicable criteria.
summaries.SB 967: Would authorize a city or county that met or exceeded its need for emergency shelter capacity and that provides committed support for interim housing, to report the number of interim housing units receiving that support that are approved, as units approved or disapproved for acutely low income households, for purposes of the annual progress report.
summaries.SB 979: Would provide that the final determination by the council of governments or the delegate subregion is subject to judicial review.
summaries.SB 996: Revises the statutory definition of a manufactured home to include structures built since June 15, 1976, with or without a foundation.
